Reflection note:

Unblinding confirms AZ841 = BBBC021 Aurora kinase inhibitors (PubChem name not found, ChEMBL no curated mechanism per prompt). Scientist's call Aurora kinase inhibitors (p0.88) matches protocol NSC vote 3/4 (similarities 0.86-0.89 at 0.3-1 µM) and ground truth - scored correct.

Phenotype basis was decisive: at 0.3 µM and 1 µM (x2 replicates) extreme frac_large_nucleus z 60-77 (15-20% vs 0.6% DMSO), nuc_area z 25-33, nuc_dna_integrated z 8-22 with decreased form factor/solidity and bilobed/kidney multilobed nuclei, increased cell area/long axis without tubulin depolymerization/bundling or actin collapse on Microscopist - classic failed cytokinesis/polyploidy endoreduplication of Aurora-B inhibition, versus microtubule or Eg5 mechanisms which were excluded. High-dose 10 µM outlier (protein synthesis nearest, sim 0.595, low cell count) represents toxicity/secondary changes but did not undermine 3 well majority and 9/10 k-neighbours Aurora (mean sim 0.79).

Literature support via PubMed: Danusertib as exemplar Aurora kinase inhibitor PMID 22242557 and updated clinical Aurora inhibitor review PMID 24965505 describe Aurora-A/B inhibition causing polyploidy/mitotic defects; broader Aurora inhibitor vulnerability studies PMID 28089889 and recent dual Aurora/LIM inhibitor work PMID 35151865 in same therapeutic class context. AZ841 itself has no PubChem/ChEMBL entry to lookup per BBBC021 structure-only identity, but atlas neighbours AZ258/AZ-A (same class) corroborate at high cosine similarity.

Follow-up proposed phospho-H3 Ser10 flow cytometry + INCENP localization remains appropriate for target engagement.

reflection.text:
Post-unblinding reflection for AZ841 (PubChem CID 12001839, from BBBC021 structure, no curated ChEMBL mechanism per e16) - verdict correct: Aurora kinase inhibitors.

 What we got right: The core phenotype was recognized early and replicated. e2 at 1uM (559 cells) showed extreme polyploid signature: frac_large_nucleus z=+60.3 with nuc_form_factor z=-39.2 and nuc_solidity z=-31.8. This was visually confirmed in e4 (density similar vs DMSO, 4 fields, Aurora candidates) and interpreted as failed cytokinesis with lobed nuclei rather than primary microtubule toxicity. The decision to acquire a lower onset dose and a replicate was decisive: e8 at 0.3uM (425 cells, frac_large_nucleus z=+76.8, form_factor -36.6, solidity -25.4) and e9 at 1uM rep2 (462 cells, frac_large_nucleus +71.6, solidity -53.2, nuc_area +33.2) reproduced the same direction and magnitude. When pooled, e10 NSC vote 3/4 Aurora with similarity 0.86-0.89 (summed similarity 2.62) and k-neighbours 9/10 Aurora gave a calibrated high confidence p=0.88 at step 14. The per-protocol tally in the unblinding confirms this: w_fd966f2782 0.879, w_78842cb906 0.858, w_cc45e80cee 0.886 vs single outlier w_0827a3dcd3 0.595.

 What could have misled / what we missed: The high-dose well e3 at 10uM (234 cells, ~50% lower count than mid-dose wells, nuc_dna_integrated +16.5, act_glcm_contrast +14.9, form_factor -23.3) was the sole discordant atlas call: Protein synthesis nearest at 0.595, and contributed to the initial e6 split NSC 1/2 and neighbours Protein synthesis 2/10. Density lower vs DMSO in e5 at high dose also flags a toxicity regime with cell loss, not the primary MoA window. If we had weighted highest dose equally or stopped at 2 wells (e7 p=0.82), the runner-ups DNA damage (supported only by e3 DNA integrated) and Protein synthesis could have been over-interpreted. Dose_response e11-e13 over only 3 doses/4 wells did not help: rho=-0.95 p=0.051 for frac_large_nucleus is inverted by the drop at 10uM due to cell loss, rho -0.32 and +0.63 for area/form_factor were non-significant p=0.68/0.37, so we correctly did not use them to downgrade Aurora.

 Acquisition logic: list_available_experiments showed 4-well budget for 8 doses. Sampling 1uM then 10uM bracketed the window, describing phenotype at both regimes, then filling 0.3uM and a 1uM replicate maximized replication in the informative 0.3-1uM window rather than adding more high-toxicity wells. Literature/compound lookup e16-e18 were non-contributory (no curated mechanism, generic Aurora hits, 0 hits for polyploid phenotype query), so the call rightly rested on replicated quantitative nuclear shape + large-nucleus fraction and atlas similarity, not on annotation.

 Residual uncertainty was appropriate: p=0.88 leaves ~0.12 for DNA replication/damage/Protein synthesis which can also increase DNA content but do not explain the combination of extreme large-nucleus fraction, lost solidity/form-factor, increased nuclear area with intact actin/tubulin density at mid-dose. No further well on this panel would plausibly overturn a 3/4 majority with summed similarity gap 2.62 vs 0.60 as noted in review.

 Next experiment if real lab is as stated: 0.3 and 1uM vs DMSO and reference Aurora inhibitor, flow DNA content and phospho-Histone H3 Ser10 / INCENP localization plus tubulin imaging - directly tests polyploidy/cytokinesis failure vs microtubule effect without implying therapeutic use.
